and their horses had grown weak and feeble from the lack of provisions,
because the plains of these regions were devoid of grass,
and the lands were in desolation,
and fodder could not be found for the horses,
nor sustenance for the men.
And because of these and such reasons, that Nawruz took it upon himself
to return in person to Baydu,
and to persuade him in whatever way possible,
so that he would not be agitated or stirred up,
and would be secure and at ease concerning the direction of Ghazan.
And when he came to Baydu,
he received him with great honor,
and revealed all his secrets to Nawruz.
So much so that this Nawruz said to Baydu:
"If you do not trust Ghazan,
and your mind is not at rest concerning him,
I will go and send you his head on a platter,"
while scheming in every way how he might escape and return to Ghazan in peace.
Baydu was overjoyed and delighted, and leaping and rejoicing he said:
"If you are truly able to do this,
I will entrust to you all the administrations of my kingdom."
And so he offered him abundant gifts,
and delivered ten thousand pieces of gold into his hands,
and wrote a diploma that he should take another ten thousand from the city of Qazvin;
and he let him go.
And when he went to Ghazan,
they began to marvel and were seized with astonishment,
at how easily that Nawruz had cast himself into the hands of Baydu,
and how Baydu, even more foolishly, had left him alive.
And from right then they began to prepare for war,
and to gather troops.
And that Nawruz personally was entrusted with the management of the armies and their gathering from every quarter.
And as for Ghazan, he sent him with a few light troops to the mountains of Mazandaran so that they might hunt there,
while the troops were being gathered in another quarter,
and he himself remained alone in one place with his household.
Baydu, however, was anxious to know:
Where were Ghazan and Nawruz? And in what, pray, were they occupied? And whether they had the intention of waging war or not? He frequently sent envoys to them,
and was contriving to probe and discover their cunning.
